before_justification: The fact-check finds that while Zahra Buhari and Kiki Osinbajo publicly supported the #EndSARS movement by sharing protest images on Instagram on October 10, 2020, there is no evidence they directly lobbied their fathers or other officials, and their actions are not identified by credible sources as a significant causal factor in the government's decision. after_justification: The fact-check refutes the claim by showing that while Zahra Buhari publicly supported the #EndSARS movement and Kiki Osinbajo allegedly lobbied privately, all official statements and reputable reporting ([Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/10/11/endsars-nigeria-dissolves-special-anti-robbery-squad), [The Cable](https://www.thecable.ng/breaking-igp-finally-disbands-sars)) attribute the dissolution of SARS directly to massive nationwide protests by Nigerian citizens, not to the daughters' actions. The daughters hold no constitutional authority to order such a dissolution, and no evidence supports their role as the cause.

October 8, 2020 marked the beginning of nationwide protests in Nigeria against the brutality of the Special Anti-Robbery Squad (SARS), a police unit established in 1992 to combat violent crime in Nigeria that had devolved into an agent of violence itself, known for its human rights abuses, especially in profiling young Nigerian men based on their perceived wealth.
